honesty 2026-10-13 (session 52): `AndroidScreenBrightnessController` checks `Settings.System.canWrite` first (clear BRIGHTNESS_PERMISSION), writes, reads the level back and reports BRIGHTNESS_SET only on a confirmed write, BRIGHTNESS_UNCHANGED when ignored, BRIGHTNESS_PERMISSION on a denied write, BRIGHTNESS_ERROR on failure. Unwired -> BRIGHTNESS_UNAVAILABLE. Never a fake success; a non-successful result fails the step via the self-evidencing rule.

manifest 2026-10-13 (session 52): `WRITE_SETTINGS` declared as a special permission with tools:ignore="ProtectedPermissions"; the user grants it from Settings. A denied grant is reported honestly (BRIGHTNESS_PERMISSION), never assumed.

report.summary: Extended Jarvis's device-control capability with a fourth backed control, `brightness` (dim/low/medium/high/max, a 0-100 percentage, or brighter/dimmer), generalising the existing `set_device_control` primitive rather than adding a new tool. A scheduled/condition automation or direct instruction can now set the display backlight via the system Settings provider, with honest read-back so an ignored or permission-denied change is reported as failure, never a fake success.

report.findings: Confirmed (high confidence): the device-control seam was explicitly designed so a new control is a mapping plus a dispatch arm, never a new tool (AGENTS.md), and further controls were a queued roadmap item - the natural next increment toward the capability bar. Confirmed: `DeviceControl.resolve` already rejects unknown (control,value) pairs, so adding `brightness` needed only a resolver branch, an executor arm, DI, a manifest permission, prompt wording and tests - low regression risk. Confirmed: brightness is a real system display setting distinct from torch/ringer/dnd, and requires the WRITE_SETTINGS special permission, which the platform enforces.
